name: Gemma 4 26B A4B (MoE, multimodal)
context_scaling: per-layer-type rope (full_attention theta 1e6 proportional / sliding_attention theta 1e4 default)
attention_variant: GQA + sliding-window/global hybrid with separate global head geometry (global_head_dim 512, num_global_key_value_heads 2)
notes: PARAMS: 25.81B is the safetensors weight count (26B nominal), including the vision tower. ACTIVE: 4B is Google's published A4B figure. KV IS DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL because the geometry is not a single formula. Gemma 4 uses TWO head geometries in the same stack: sliding-window layers have head_dim 256 with 8 KV heads, while global layers have global_head_dim 512 with only 2 global KV heads (num_global_key_value_heads). Per global layer that is 2 * 512 = 1024 KV elements versus 8 * 256 = 2048 for a sliding layer, and there are 5 global layers out of 30. A correct figure needs both geometries and the PLE/vision allocation, which config.json does not fully resolve. Deriving a single number here would be a guess. ROUTING: num_experts 128, top_k_experts 8. Eight of 128 is a higher active fraction than gpt-oss's 4 of 128, so routing compute is a bigger share of per-token FLOPs than in gpt-oss despite the smaller active count. moe_intermediate_size 704 against a 2816 hidden size makes each expert very narrow. MEMORY IS SET BY TOTAL, NOT ACTIVE: Google's own doc states all 26B must be resident for fast routing, and puts the BF16 footprint at 57.7 GB (28.8 GB at SFP8, 14.4 GB at Q4_0). active_params_b=4 therefore describes compute per token, not memory. This is the same trap as gpt-oss-120b, stated explicitly by the vendor. attention_k_eq_v=true means K and V share storage in the global layers, which is a real KV reduction independent of head count. final_logit_softcapping=30.0 is retained from Gemma 2. All Gemma 4 sizes ship an MTP draft model for speculative decoding (Google's doc), which changes the decode FLOP mix.
